doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Choosing San Francisco over New York
summary: He found New York too intense, disliked the weather, and fell in love with San Francisco during a 1963 fellowship at Langley Porter.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That I think must be one of the reasons that he kept it on his playlist for so long. It does fit him well, I would say that. Why didn’t you stay in New York?

I toyed with it. In some ways it would have been easier to keep a higher profile musical career going had I stayed in New York. But back then the vibe in New York I found too intense and oppressive. I have plenty of internal energy. I don’t need that press from outside so much. And I hated the weather. I grew up in the Midwest with the extremes of temperature of Chicago. And by the time I left to go to medical school I’d had my fill of © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

blisteringly hot, humid summers and cold, austere, windy winters. I wanted a temperate climate. So when I had a fellowship in 1963, before this one in New York, which was to go out to San Francisco to the Langley Porter Psychiatric Institute for the summer, I fell in love with San Francisco. The first night I was here I had rented an apartment on the top of Twin Peaks and I’m looking down over this whole city, and I’m thinking boy, I may never leave this place. And when it came time to apply for internship I applied to six hospitals in the San Francisco Bay area. Nowhere else. That was it. And I have never been sorry. I love living out here.
This is the first time for me and I can see what you mean so far.

Yeah it’s been just right, although certainly there is a sacrifice. If you live right in New York where all that foment is and there’s a lot of business opportunities always, networking and stuff, it would have been easier to keep a higher profile going. But I really was more concerned with the overall quality that my life would have and the balance and trying to maintain a balance, and really at the hub of all of it I feel is my life with my wife Josephine. We’ve been together for 35 years. And that seems at the hub and then all these other things are, you know the spokes.
